Typical-day pedestrian profile for chosen sensors and years

Source: R/hourly_profile.R
hourly_profile.Rd

Selects the average hourly pedestrian counts for the sensors, years and day type you choose, so you can compare the shape of a typical day across places and years. This is the table behind the app's "typical day" chart.

Usage

hourly_profile(
  sensors,
  years,
  day = c("Weekday", "Weekend"),
  data = ped_hourly
)

Arguments

sensors

Integer vector of sensor location_id values to keep. See ped_sensors for the available IDs.

years

Integer vector of years to keep.

day

Which kind of day to show: "Weekday" (Monday to Friday) or "Weekend" (Saturday and Sunday). Defaults to "Weekday".

data

A data frame with the same columns as ped_hourly. Defaults to ped_hourly.

Value

A data frame with one row per sensor, year and hour, containing location_id, sensor_name, year, day_type, hour, mean_count and n_days. If none of the chosen sensors and years have data, a data frame with zero rows is returned, so callers can show a helpful message.

Examples

# Busiest sensor in the data, weekdays in the latest year
top_sensor <- ped_hourly[which.max(ped_hourly$mean_count), "location_id"][[1]]
hourly_profile(sensors = top_sensor, years = max(ped_hourly$year), day = "Weekday")
